newsitem.title: HONG KONG: US chamber of commerce in HK to push for China MFN.
newsitem.headline: US chamber of commerce in HK to push for China MFN.

text.p: The American Chamber of Commerce in Hong Kong said it will send a delegation to Washington next week to argue for permanent extension of China's Most Favoured Nation (MFN) trading privileges.
"It is important that the case for permanent MFN be argued forcefully and clearly," Douglas Henck, chamber chairman said in a statement received by Reuters on Friday.

"The ongoing debate over MFN for China is counterproductive to the overall Sino-American relationship and harmful to Hong Kong," said Henck, leader of the delegation that plans to meet senior United States officials and members of the House and Senate during the May 12-16 visit.
U.S. President Bill Clinton has until June to decide on MFN, and Congress must then ratify that decision.
"Revocation of MFN would seriously damage Hong Kong's economy, undermining confidence during a critical transition period," Henck said.
Britain hands back Hong Kong to China on July 1, ending more than 150 years of colonial rule.

Victor Fung, chairman of the Hong Kong Trade Development Council, said in Washington on Monday the United States could help Hong Kong most after the handover by keeping its markets open to the territory's products and services.
The council is a government-funded trade promotion body.

Hong Kong's government has said a withdrawal of China's MFN status would cut Hong Kong's gross domestic product growth by between two and 2.8 percentage points, and lead to a loss of 61,000 to 86,000 jobs.
Hong Kong serves as a major gateway for exports and imports for China, and many Hong Kong manufacturers have moved their production bases to the mainland to take advantage of lower production costs.
